parsed.why: No criminalisation and strong hate-crime law, but recurring oversight findings of birth-sex custody placement, isolation and strip-search exposure unremedied; 64% of trans respondents report discrimination; dated border and hostel incidents. Universal-exposure gaps hold it in Elevated Risk.

Section 379 criminalises male attire 'in the fashion of a woman' on appearance alone; police documented harassing, arresting and torturing LGBTQ people; minister urged arrests; no protections; most openly LGBTQ citizens have fled.

State-directed targeting: 377 enforced as aggravating factor, 'shadow law' used specifically against trans women, documented strip-searches, beating, sexual violence in custody, extortion, post-coup killings, no recognition or recourse, 'avoid entirely'.

Constitutional gender-identity protection, bathroom access protected, hate-crime and discrimination law, lowest regional victimisation, working courts (prison damages awarded). Deductions: institutional lag in prisons, pending border-detention case, low police reporting.

No criminalisation, but no GI protection, no recognition, documented refusal of medical care including hormones and general treatment, unpunished anti-LGBT violence with thin recourse, police avoided from fear, rural hostility. High Risk.
